name: Colorist
description: Samples the dominant colour of frames across a video and renders them as a vertical-stripe movie barcode, stored beside the media and shown at the foot of the detail page.

versions.changelog: Fixes three problems found on a live server. The barcode image now displays: it is loaded by an tag, which cannot send an Authorization header, so the endpoint answered every request with 401 and both the settings preview and the detail-page strip rendered as broken images — the access token now travels in the query string. Frame analysis is capped at the requested stripe count: -skip_frame nokey turned out to be only a hint, and a 110-minute 2160p film was delivering 157,791 frames for a 1,000-stripe barcode, so every frame was scaled and colour-clustered for nothing. HDR and Dolby Vision are converted before their colours are measured, rather than being decoded as though they were SDR — which read far too dark and far too grey, and made every 4K HDR title produce a muted strip. Dolby Vision profile 5, which has no HDR10 base layer and decodes pink and green, is converted with libplacebo so its metadata is actually applied; profiles 7 and 8 use the standard HDR path. If a required ffmpeg filter is missing, sampling falls back a step at a time and logs it rather than producing nothing.
